record.title: SpeechT-RAG: Reliable Depression Detection in LLMs with Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Speech Timing Information
A Survey of LLM-based Agents in Medicine: How far are we from Baymax?
SpeechT-RAG: Reliable Depression Detection in LLMs with Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Speech Timing Information
record.reason: Formal long-paper type awaiting independent reconciliation. Core clinical mental-health task: SpeechT-RAG uses durations between acoustic landmarks for depression classification and confidence estimation, with medical reasoning and experiments focused throughout on depression-associated speech timing. Section 5 evaluates DAIC-WOZ clinical interviews (107 training and 35 development interviews); the reported results are on the development set, not an independent clinical deployment cohort. Section 3 compares depressed/non-depressed timing distributions and Section 4 evaluates calibrated confidence. This is medical-primary, not a generic RAG test with incidental health data; the findings do not establish clinical diagnostic safety.
